title: Spark brieflet: concept catalog for lightweight first-run onramp
content:
Context / why this note exists:

Quick brain-dump of compact ideas for a really small 'first-run' onramp that gets teams to a meaningful Redwood inference experience within 5–10 minutes. Goal is a low-friction path for new developer signups that demonstrates latency, cost controls, and a simple workflow for testing prompts. This is intentionally lightweight — think minimal screens, a single canonical example, and fast feedback loops.

Problem statements:
- Too many new teams drop off because the first experiment requires too many choices (model, quantization, batching, network config).
- Early impressions hinge on 1) latency and 2) obvious cost guardrails. If either feels risky, devs bail.
- We want to convert quick experiments into long-term usage (hosted -> dedicated). Need a replicable onboarding that surfaces value and next steps.

Primary goals (measurable):
- 30% higher conversion from sign-up -> first successful generation (defined by API call + returned tokens) within 10 minutes.
- Median first-call latency < 300ms for the example experience in US region.
- Provide clear cost estimate shown before first call and a default soft cap.
- 20% of first-call users opt in to a follow-up setup (email + sample workload import).

Constraints / design principles:
- Single canonical flow: the fewer toggles we show, the better.
- Default to a safe, cost-efficient model variant (quantized, cached) but allow an explicit "faster/bigger" toggle for curious devs.
- Instrument everything: step-by-step telemetry so we can diagnose where users drop.
- Keep the UI copy engineering-centric and terse. Target persona: backend or ML engineer trying out integration.

Proposed flow (minimal screens):
1) Quick landing (lightweight): headline, 2 bullets (latency, cost), CTA "Try a quick example".
2) Single example card: small editable prompt, sample system instruction, model & region hidden but readable under "advanced".
3) Cost & latency preview: approximate cost per 1k tokens and expected median latency for this model/region. Soft cap default $5/day (user-adjustable).
4) Run -> live stream response (token streaming) shown inline plus simple timeline of latency and token-count.
5) Post-run actions: "Save this snippet", "Export curl/SDK snippet", "Add to project" (creates project stub), "Request dedicated trial" CTA.

User stories (rough):
- As a new dev, I want to try a pre-filled prompt so I can validate the API without wiring my app.
- As an engineer, I want to see an estimated cost before I run so I don't accidentally spin up expensive usage.
- As a product lead, I want to capture the first successful demo and tie it to an account so sales can offer a dedicated capacity trial.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- A single pre-filled example flow that executes an API call end-to-end without exposing advanced configuration.
- The flow shows an estimated cost and a configurable soft cap prior to execution.
- Streaming UI renders tokens as they arrive; SDK/cURL snippet produced after run includes the soft cap metadata header.
- Telemetry events emitted for: landing view, example edit, run attempt, run success/failure, opt-in CTA clicks.

Metrics to track:
- Time from signup -> first run attempt (target < 10 min).
- Success rate of first run (target +30% relative to baseline).
- Percent of users who expand "advanced" (low means defaults work).
- Median latency and token cost for first run.
- Downstream action rate (save snippet, export, create project).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Defaults mask real production behavior (customers frustrated later). Mitigation: show "why this is a safe default" microcopy linking to a quick explainer and a clear path to ramping up model capacity.
- Risk: Billing surprises if soft caps are ignored. Mitigation: soft cap implemented in control plane with explicit Opt-In override logs + mandatory email confirmation for >$20/day.
- Risk: Streaming complexity on edge networks. Mitigation: fallback to non-streaming response and surface the reason in telemetry.

Implementation notes / infra hooks:
- Reuse existing streaming UI components in console repo (PR branch: feature/streaming-compact-run).
- Feature flag gating: experiments:onramp_quickrun. Ensure telemetry schema includes session_id and sample_id.
- Add light-weight default model variant to model catalog: onboard-small-v1 (quantized, prefetched KV cache). Needs a serving runtime profile so routing picks low-latency nodes.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Do we auto-create a sample project or require explicit click? (tradeoff: conversion vs noise in project list).
- Where to surface the opt-in for follow-up (modal vs inline)? Quick test: show inline after success with a checkbox.
- Should the soft cap be per-day or per-run? Per-day easier to reason about, but per-run safer. Lean per-day for UX simplicity, with per-run controls for advanced users.

Next short-term experiments (A/B candidates):
A) CTA copy: "Try example" vs "Run in your app" (affects conversion).
B) Soft cap default $5 vs $10 (affects opt-outs and trial usage).
C) Auto-create project vs manual create (affects downstream activation rate).

Immediate TODOs:
- [ ] Draft a tiny microcopy set for landing, example card, cost preview (owner: Mira)
- [ ] Add model variant stub to model-catalog (owner: Ravi)
- [ ] Wire telemetry events and sketch schema (owner: Evelyn)
- [ ] Spike: half-day front-end prototype using existing streaming UI (owner: Harper)
- [ ] Create JIRA epic and link from this note -> JIRA:PROD-4123

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Could reuse the "export curl" workflow to include an ephemeral API key limited to snippet runs. Low-friction demo with automatic expiry.
- Consider a one-click "simulate production" preview that runs same prompt with a bigger model and shows delta in latency & cost. Good for showing uplift and next-paid step.
- Keep copy frankly technical; avoid onboarding templates aimed at non-devs for this flow.

If we get time for a slightly larger scope (v1+): add a tiny UX for importing a sample dataset (CSV of prompts) and running 3 quick evaluations to show quality/cost tradeoffs. But MVP should be single-prompt, one-click, streaming, cost-safeguarded.

End of jot — will iterate once we have telemetry baseline and prototype feedback.
